briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B as National Psychedelic Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's legal market just surpassed $17 billion in combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales, and Ann Arbor keeps adding storefronts even as operators push the governor's race for relief on the 24% wholesale tax. Nationally, the FDA's landmark psychedelic hearing and Compass Pathways' on-track 2027 launch show real momentum building from setback into buildout.

local.text: New Standard opens the doors in Ann Arbor — New Standard Ann Arbor offered giveaways and discounts on its opening weekend Sept. 3-6, adding fresh retail energy to one of the state's most competitive dispensary markets.

Michigan's market crosses $17 billion cumulative — the CRA's latest monthly report shows combined adult-use and medical sales have generated an estimated $2.66 billion in state excise and sales taxes since regulated sales began, proof demand hasn't cracked despite the new tax.

Jars Cannabis wins its surveillance-camera fight — the 54-store chain got Madison Heights to take down a police-monitored Flock camera aimed at its parking lot after mounting a sign to block its view and negotiating with the city, a rare operator win against local overreach.

Industry group bets on a tax-cut candidate — the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association officially endorsed Republican gubernatorial nominee John James, calling him the clear choice for his commitment to repealing the 24% wholesale tax, giving operators a real path to relief this November.

Tax pain persists, but operators are adapting — Higher Love closed five of its nine Upper Peninsula stores citing the tax, while three-store rival Rize has sustained growth by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers instead of absorbing the hit alone.

national.text: FDA holds its first psychedelic-therapy hearing — the Sept. 14 hearing marked one of the most consequential regulatory moments for psychedelic-assisted therapy to date, with MAPS sharing its open-science ibogaine data with FDA, HHS and VA officials.

Compass Pathways stays on track for 2027 launch — the rolling NDA submission for COMP360 remains on schedule for completion in Q4 2026, with commercial launch anticipated in the first half of 2027 pending FDA approval and DEA rescheduling.

Curaleaf's Aurora bid signals cross-border ambition — Curaleaf announced a $4-per-share takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis on August 10 and formally commenced the offer August 18, a 45% premium creating $1.5 billion-plus in pro forma combined revenue.

Federal court upholds medical marijuana rescheduling — reclassification opponents' lawsuit to stop medical marijuana's Schedule III change was rebuffed this week, with the D.C. Circuit leaving the rescheduling order in effect on Sept. 9, 2026.

Appeals court reversal exposes rescheduling's gap — a federal appeals court wiped out a $32 million verdict a Michigan grower won against two Curaleaf subsidiaries, finding that executing the sales contract required committing a federal crime since marijuana remains Schedule I for adult-use — the exact problem full rescheduling is meant to fix.
